newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan Housing Bank pre-tax profits stead.
newsitem.headline: Jordan Housing Bank pre-tax profits stead.

text.p: Jordan's Housing Bank, the country's second largest bank, said on Wednesday its pre-tax profits rose 2.4 percent in 1996 to 10.5 million dinars ($14.83 million) bolstered by steady commercial business growth.
"This growth in the balance sheet has been attained as a natural result of the growth in all the main financial indicators," Zuhair Khoury, the bank's chairman said in a statement.

The sale of two main tourism and one bank shareholding in its stock market portfolio accounted for its high 9.45 million dinars net profit in 1995. Its pre-tax profits stood at 10.25 million dinars in 1995. The bank still remains the largest single, non-government investor on Jordan's stock market.

The bank's assets grew in 1996 to 1.136 billion dinars against 1.103 billion dinars in 1995. Reserves stood at 56.3 million dinars or nearly double its 25 million dinar capital. The capital base was doubled in 1995 from 12 million dinars in two stages by reserves capitalisation and private placement.

Shareholders' equity rose to 81.3 million dinars in 1996 from 77.8 million dinars in 1995, second only to Arab Bank among Jordan's 20 private banks. The government owns around 18 percent and Kuwait's state-owned Kuwait Real Estate Investment Group a 20.6 percent stake with equal 6 percent stakes by Oman, Qatar and Iran. The remaining is held by local and private investors.
Housing Bank, which has 121 branches across Jordan, is the main provider of private real estate credit and ranks second among the country's banks in size of assets and deposits.
The bank's accumulative loans topped 2.266 billion dinars, of which 1.095 billion dinars were housing loans covering 21.4 percent of construction permits in the kingdom.
Its outstanding loans portfolio rose to 661.1 million dinars from 622.9 million dinars with the bank's commercial loans now exceeding its former mainly real estate credit.
Housing Bank's strategic focus is to expand into comprehensive banking away from real estate credit, its original niche when it was first set up in 1973, bank officials said.
Housing Bank's total deposits in 1996 stood at 918 million dinars from 885.7 million dinars in 1995.
The bank, which has two branches in Palestinian self-rule areas in Ramallah and Gaza, plans to expand its presence with a third branch in Nablus in the first quarter of 1997.
It has applied to the Palestinian Monetary Authority to set up new branches in Hebron, Bethlehem, Beireh and Arab East Jerusalem suburbs.
The bank, setting its eyes on the Palestinian real estate market, is planning to jointly set up with the Palestinian Authority and investors a Housing Bank on the Jordanian model.
Housing Bank also plans, in line with foreign exchange liberalisation moves, to expand its investment and private banking business for its clients in capital markets.
The bank registered in Bahrain a 20 million dinar fund in Jordanian blue chip and newly established companies.
The fund, the first of its kind by a local financial institution, will be managed by New York based Alliance Capital. Housing Bank now markets 14 of its global funds locally,

The Jordan fund, which the bank plans to launch in the first quarter of 1997, targets mainly foreign investors. It is to be listed on both the Amman bourse and the Bahrain Stock Exchange under a cross listing deal.
